_artifactRules_readme: THE ONE ARTIFACT LIST, IN THE ORDER THE ARTIFACTS MUST BE WRITTEN.
The array order IS the write order, and `dependsOn` names WHY an
artifact waits for another. The order is not a convention: every edge
carries the fact that must pass forward, and the floor proves that join
PLAN_TASK_COVERAGE). Writing the dependent first is not a style
preference — it is a content inconsistency the moment it is written.
`dependsOn[].family` is a rule's `pattern` — the FAMILY identity the
floor already matches against, so a plan may name its files as it
likes. `hard: true` means the dependent CANNOT be written correctly
without the dependency, and the one-file scaffold cursor refuses it
until the dependency exists; `hard: false` is a convention that orders
An edge DISSOLVES when the profile omits the dependency (there is
nothing to wait for) and becomes EXTERNAL when the profile reuses it
(the host document satisfies it — cite it, never regenerate it).

_classes_readme: The artifact set is NOT listed here: profile.artifactRules is the only list.

SMALL.label: SMALL — add or touch a few things
notes: Every task entry STILL carries repo-root-relative paths verbatim in file_ownership, in each step, and in verification commands.
No Context section, no diagrams, no PRD, no architecture contract, no ADRs.

MEDIUM.label: MEDIUM — a real feature with real risk
requires: per-task sections with approach + edge cases + out-of-scope
notes: One `<id> — <title>` heading per task, in dependency order.
Verification steps are repo-root-relative (no `../`, no `--plan .`), exact, and runnable.
architecture.yaml is created ONLY when the profile finds a cross-module or contract trigger; the scaffold serves it when it is marked create.

LARGE.label: LARGE — a full professional stack (greenfield from scratch)
requires: docs/prd.md when the profile marks it create (~1 page per major module)
architecture.yaml with naming_conventions, data_contracts, api_contracts and environment_matrix
an edge-case matrix per task (every row maps to an acceptance bullet)
per-module diagrams only when the profile marks them create (<=15 nodes each) plus one integration diagram
notes: Requirement ids (FR-<MODULE>-nn) are defined in docs/prd.md and cited from tasks.yaml acceptance lines.
architecture.yaml is the anti-hallucination source of truth: tasks cite its keys instead of restating shapes from memory.
Every artifact is conditional on the profile: a LARGE plan may reuse an existing PRD or architecture document, and must record that decision.
